subject_lessons.title: Y7 Math: Linear Equations (y = mx + b) & Probability (0.0 to 1.0)
subject_lessons.story:
TRADITIONAL MATH LESSON (GRADE 7):
• A Linear Equation `y = m * x + b` has a Slope `m` (rate of change) and a y-intercept `b` (bias!).
  Notice that a single neuron computes `z = w * x + b`—the weight `w` IS the slope `m`, and the bias `b` IS the intercept!
• Probability ranges from `0.0` (impossible) to `1.0` (certain). In RL, `epsilon = 0.15` means a 15% chance of exploring!

# 📐 YEAR 7 MATH ASSIGNMENT: y = mx + b as a Single Neuron
w_slope = 2.5
b_intercept = -0.4
for x in [-1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 2.0]:
    y = w_slope * x + b_intercept
    print(f'x = {x:4.1f} -> y = {w_slope}*{x} + ({b_intercept}) = {y:5.2f}')

subject_lessons.subject: science
subject_lessons.title: Y7 Science: Newton's Three Laws of Motion (F = ma) & Natural Selection
subject_lessons.story:
TRADITIONAL SCIENCE LESSON (GRADE 7):
• Newton's 1st Law (Inertia): An object in motion stays in motion unless acted on by a net force.
• Newton's 2nd Law: Force = Mass × Acceleration (`F = m * a`, so `a = F / m`).
• Newton's 3rd Law: Every action has an equal and opposite reaction (rocket exhaust pushes down; rocket accelerates up!).
• Darwin's Natural Selection: Organisms with beneficial genetic traits survive and pass their genes to offspring.

subject_lessons.story:
TRADITIONAL LANGUAGE ARTS LESSON (GRADE 7):
In persuasive and scientific writing, avoid Logical Fallacies:
• False Cause (Correlation vs. Causation): Just because two events happen together doesn't mean one caused the other! To prove causation in science and AI, change ONE variable at a time (a Controlled Experiment).

# 🤖 YEAR 7 AI CAPSTONE: Anti-Hover Reward Shaping
def compute_reward(dist_to_pad: float, speed: float, landed: bool) -> float:
    shaping = -110.0 * dist_to_pad - 45.0 * speed - 0.06
    return shaping + (260.0 if landed else 0.0)

print('Hovering high:', round(compute_reward(0.8, 0.1, False), 1))
print('Soft landing: ', round(compute_reward(0.0, 0.05, True), 1))
assert compute_reward(0.0, 0.05, True) > compute_reward(0.8, 0.1, False)
